title: Omani legend, US novice: Pakistan recovers bodies from Broad Peak - Al Jazeera
description: Omani legend, US novice: Pakistan recovers bodies from Broad Peak  Al Jazeera
publisher.title: Al Jazeera
full_article:
Rescuers continue the search for six climbers still missing after an avalanche hit Pakistan’s Broad Peak, as officials identified one of the four recovered bodies as Nadhira Al Harthy, the first Omani woman to summit Mount Everest.

Pakistani authorities recovered three of the bodies on Friday in harsh weather that hampered flights by search and rescue helicopters, officials said, and identified them as Nepalese climber Pur Bahadur Gurung and American climber Sarah Mallory Geis, as well as Harthy.

The officials did not immediately identify the fourth body that was found.

The expedition comprised five Nepali climbers, the Omani and American climbers, Pakistani climber Sohail Sakhi, a Chinese climber identified only as Wang, and one other foreign climber, according to the Alpine Club of Pakistan.

The expedition leader was the renowned mountaineer Nirmal Purja, a Nepal-born former soldier in the British army widely known as Nims Dai. He climbed the world’s 14 highest peaks in a record 189 days in 2019, an achievement featured in the Netflix documentary, 14 Peaks: Nothing is Impossible. His record was surpassed in 2023.

A file photo of Nirmal Purja, one of the team members of the all-Nepalese mountaineering team that became the first to scale Mount K2 in winter, gestures as the team arrives at Tribhuvan International Airport in Kathmandu, Nepal on January 26, 2021 [Niranjan Shrestha/AP Photo]

The climbers were swept away in an avalanche on the 8,051-metre (26,414ft) peak, the world’s 12th-highest mountain, about midday on Thursday. The area in which the search is taking place is “remote and difficult”, said Sajid Hussain, deputy director of the tourism department in Gilgit-Baltistan.

Of the world’s 14 highest peaks, eight are in Nepal, five in Pakistan and one in Tibet. Climbing experts say barely more than three dozen mountaineers have climbed all 14 peaks to date. Broad Peak is considered one of Pakistan’s most challenging climbs.

Nepal’s Gurung, known to his friends as Yukta, climbed Everest more times than anyone else from the Gurung community, with 10 successful ascents to his name, Nepal’s Online Khabar noted. He also successfully climbed 12 of the world’s 8,000-metre (26,246ft) peaks.

Yukta had also set a record by summiting Pakistan’s K2, the world’s second-highest peak, within 24 hours. He was regularly involved in rescue operations for tourists stranded in the mountains.

Oman’s Al Harthy held a master’s degree in geography and previously served as director of the Citizenship Department at Oman’s Ministry of Education, Gulf News reported. In 2019, she became the first Omani woman to reach the summit of Mount Everest, and then the first Omani to climb K2, the world’s second-highest mountain.

For the US’s Geis, it was her first try at an 8,000-metre peak in Pakistan.

Geis, 39, lived in San Antonio. She announced on social media earlier this year that she was closing her Pilates studio to take “a giant leap of faith into the unknown to see where life goes. I have a sneaking suspicion there will be lots of helmets, harnesses, and crampons involved.”

Sakhi was a guide for the company, as well as a geographer and high-altitude photographer who had climbed several of the world’s major peaks.

अमेरिका केरऽ गेस लेली ई हुनकऽ पहलऽ कोशिश छेलै कि पाकिस्तान म॑ ८,००० मीटर के चोटी प॑ पहुँचै के कोशिश करलऽ गेलै ।

सखी कंपनी केरऽ गाइड छेलै, साथ ही साथ भूगोलविद आरू उच्च ऊंचाई वाला फोटोग्राफर भी छेली जे दुनिया केरऽ कई प्रमुख चोटी प॑ चढ़ी गेलऽ छेलै ।

title: Nirmal Purja, who redrew the limits of human endurance and reshaped Nepali mountaineering, dies in Broad Peak avalanche - The Kathmandu Post
description: Nirmal Purja, who redrew the limits of human endurance and reshaped Nepali mountaineering, dies in Broad Peak avalanche  The Kathmandu Post
publisher.title: The Kathmandu Post
full_article:
Nirmal Purja, the Nepal-born former special forces soldier who stunned the mountaineering world by summiting all 14 of the planet’s 8,000-metre peaks in six months, has died in an avalanche on Pakistan’s Broad Peak. He was 43. Purja's death was confirmed in a statement by Elite Expedition on its social account on Saturday. "It is with profound sadness and immense heartbreak that we confirm that Nirmal "Nimsdai" Purja tragically lost his life following the avalanche on Broad Peak," the statement said. "We have also received confirmation that other members of the expedition sadly did not survive." Purja was on Broad Peak as part of an expedition when an avalanche struck the team on July 30, 2026. Pakistani mountaineering authorities said there had been no communication with the group since the incident. Mingma Gyabu Sherpa, a member of Nepal’s House of Representatives and Purja’s business partner, had said that tracking data showed Purja’s position had shifted after the avalanche — first appearing to have been swept downhill, then moving again from where the signal had stopped. Known across Nepal and the global climbing world as “Nims Dai,” Purja became one of the most recognisable figures in modern mountaineering after completing what he called Project Possible — an attempt, in 2019, to climb all 14 of the world’s eight-thousanders in seven months. He finished in six months and six days, shattering a previous record by more than seven years. Purja spent much of his career testing the outer limits of human endurance, driven by an unshakeable belief that anything was achievable if a person set their mind to it.

Photo: Courtesy of Nirmal Purja's Facebook

“I am quite lucky with my physiology but I have also been trained by the best unit on earth,” he told the Post in an interview in 2019, referring to his military training. “So when you combine that with a positive mindset, you can do anything.” Purja was born on July 25, 1983, in Dana village in Myagdi district, and grew up largely in Chitwan. He came from a family with a long history of military service: his father and three older brothers all served in Nepal’s Gurkha regiments. Purja followed that path himself, serving six years as a British Gurkha before becoming the first Nepali to be accepted into the British Special Boat Service, an elite unit of the Royal Navy. “Being a Gurkha was my only dream,” he wrote in his book. “It was the only thing I wanted to do.” Across a military career spanning roughly 16 years, he later became a subject-matter expert in extreme cold-weather warfare within the SBS’s mountain unit. He was appointed a Member of the Order of the British Empire (MBE) in 2018 for his military service and mountaineering achievements. On the morning of October 30, 2019, Tribhuvan International Airport in Kathmandu was packed with journalists waiting for him. Purja emerged from the arrival hall buried under flower garlands so heavy he could barely move his neck. To finance that expedition, Purja resigned from the Special Boat Service, gave up his military pension and sold his house in the UK. “I gave up my job in the United Kingdom. I gave up my pension and sold my house for this high-altitude, high-speed quest,” he told reporters at the time. “Nobody believed it could be done. Everyone was laughing at me when I launched Project Possible.” Purja did not come to mountaineering through a conventional path. His climbing career traces back to a 2012 trek to Everest Base Camp, originally planned as a simple hike, that he extended into a summit push, an experience he later said had ignited his ambition for the mountains. He went on to compress what typically takes climbers years or decades into months. His 2019 record-breaking expedition, chronicled in the Netflix documentary “14 Peaks: Nothing Is Impossible,” carried him across Nepal, Pakistan and Tibet, closing with Shishapangma on October 29, 2019. His team included Mingma David Sherpa, Gesman Tamang, Galjen Sherpa, Lakpa Dendi Sherpa and Halung Dorchi Sherpa.

Photo: Courtesy of Nirmal Purja's Facebook

For Purja, the record was never simply about speed. On April 23, 2019, while descending Annapurna, Purja interrupted his own expedition to help rescue Malaysian climber Chin Wui Kin, who had been stranded without food, water or supplemental oxygen for around 40 hours. Purja brought him down, though Chin later died from his injuries after being evacuated to Singapore. Weeks later, during the ascent of Kanchenjunga, Purja again gave up his own summit push to help others. “At 8,450 metres, we had to give our oxygen and start rescuing three other climbers,” he recalled. “That was a suicidal attempt and probably the hardest moment.” His final obstacle on the expedition came not from weather or altitude but politics: with only Shishapangma left to climb, Chinese authorities repeatedly delayed his climbing permit, which was finally granted on October 15 after Nepal’s government intervened diplomatically with Beijing. “From rescuing people at high altitudes to fixing ropes, from supplying oxygen to opening routes and going nights without sleeping, we were doing multiple jobs and were testing our limits,” Purja said afterward. “But we delivered.” Purja called the feat “extremely, horrendously good,” despite setbacks along the way, including having his oxygen supply stolen while climbing Lhotse. Speaking to reporters in Kathmandu after his return, Purja said he hoped his record would show the next generation of Nepali climbers that “anything is possible with determination.” In doing so, he broke South Korean climber Kim Chang-ho’s previous record of seven years, ten months and six days, and eclipsed Polish climbing legend Jerzy Kukuczka, who had become the first person to complete all 14 eight-thousanders, in 1987, after nearly eight years. Purja’s own record proved short-lived: on July 27, 2023, Norwegian climber Kristin Harila and her Nepali climbing partner, Tenjen (Lama) Sherpa, completed all 14 peaks in just 92 days. His 2019 schedule bordered on the unbelievable. He climbed Annapurna and Dhaulagiri, moved to Kanchenjunga, then summited Everest, immediately traversed to adjoining Lhotse, flew to Makalu Base Camp and climbed Makalu — all within 48 hours. His campaign then continued through Pakistan, where he climbed Nanga Parbat, Gasherbrum I, Gasherbrum II, Broad Peak and K2, before returning to Nepal to finish Manaslu, Cho Oyu and, finally, Shishapangma. During that same expedition, Purja took a photograph that would become one of the defining mountaineering images of the decade: a long queue of climbers near Everest’s summit, widely described as a “traffic jam,” which ran on front pages worldwide, including in The Kathmandu Post, and helped push Nepal’s government to tighten climbing regulations. He later co-founded Elite Exped with Mingma David Sherpa and, in January 2021, was part of a 10-member all-Nepali team, alongside Mingma Gyalje Sherpa, that achieved the first winter ascent of K2 — one of the last unclaimed milestones in Himalayan mountaineering, a peak he told The Post was the only one among the 14 that genuinely scared him. His journey reached a global audience beyond Nepal in 2021, when the documentary “14 Peaks: Nothing Is Impossible” introduced viewers in 191 countries to Nepal’s climbing community and made Purja one of the world’s most recognisable mountaineers almost overnight. Purja published a memoir, “Beyond Possible” in 2020, tracing his path from a 16-year military career to record-setting mountaineer, and continued to add to his list of Guinness World Records in high-altitude climbing in the years that followed.

पाकिस्तान केरऽ ब्रॉड पीक प॑ हिमस्खलन म॑ ग्रह केरऽ ८,००० मीटर केरऽ सब १४ चोटी प॑ पहुँची क॑ पर्वतारोहण जगत क॑ स्तब्ध करी दै वाला नेपाल म॑ जन्मलऽ विशेष बल केरऽ पूर्व सैनिक निर्मल पुरजा के मौत होय गेलऽ छै । हुनकऽ उम्र ४३ साल छेलै ।शनिदिन एलिट एक्सपीडिएशन न॑ अपनऽ सोशल अकाउंट प॑ जारी बयान म॑ पुरजा केरऽ मौत के पुष्टि करलकै । बयान मँ कहलौ गेलौ छै कि गहरा उदासी आरू अपार दिल टूटै के साथ हम्मं॑ ई बात के पुष्टि करै छियै कि ब्रॉड पीक प॑ हिमस्खलन के बाद निर्मल "निम्सदाई" पुरजा न॑ दुखद रूप स॑ जान गंवाय देलकै । "हमरा सब क॑ ई बात के पुष्टि भी मिललऽ छै कि ई अभियान केरऽ अन्य सदस्य दुखद रूप स॑ नै बचलै ।" पुरजा एकटा अभियान के हिस्सा के तौर पर ब्रॉड पीक पर छल जखन 30 जुलाई 2026 के टीम पर हिमस्खलन भेल छल.पाकिस्तानी पर्वतारोहण अधिकारी के कहनाय छनि जे एहि घटना के बाद सं एहि समूह सं कोनो संवाद नहिं भेल अछि. नेपाल केरऽ प्रतिनिधि सभा के सदस्य आरू पुर्जा केरऽ बिजनेस पार्टनर मिंगमा ग्याबू शेर्पा न॑ कहल॑ छेलै कि ट्रैकिंग डाटा स॑ पता चलै छै कि हिमस्खलन के बाद पुरजा केरऽ स्थिति बदली गेलऽ छै — पहल॑ ऐन्हऽ लगै छै कि ओकरा नीचें बहाय देलऽ गेलऽ छै, फेरू वू जगह स॑ फेरू बढ़ी रहलऽ छै, जहां सिग्नल बंद होय गेलऽ छेलै । पूरा नेपाल आरू वैश्विक पर्वतारोहण जगत म॑ “निम्स दाई” के नाम स॑ जानलऽ जाय वाला पुरजा, जेकरा हुनी प्रोजेक्ट पॉसिबल कहलकै — ओकरा पूरा करला के बाद आधुनिक पर्वतारोहण केरऽ सबसें पहचानऽ वाला हस्ती म॑ स॑ एक बनलै — एगो प्रयास, २०१९ म॑, सात महीना म॑ दुनिया केरऽ सब १४ आठ-हजारऽ प॑ चढ़ै के । ओ छह मास छह दिन मे समाप्त केलनि आ पहिने के रिकॉर्ड सात साल सं बेसी के तोड़ि देलखिन्ह. पुरजा अपनऽ कैरियर केरऽ बहुत हिस्सा मानव सहनशक्ति केरऽ बाहरी सीमा के परीक्षण म॑ बिताबै छेलै, जेकरा म॑ ई अटल विश्वास छेलै कि अगर कोय व्यक्ति अपनऽ दिमाग ओकरा प॑ लगाबै छै त॑ कोय भी चीज साध्य होय सकै छै ।

फोटो : निर्मल पुरजा के फेसबुक से सौजन्य

अपनऽ सैन्य प्रशिक्षण के जिक्र करतें हुअ॑ २०१९ म॑ पोस्ट क॑ देलऽ गेलऽ साक्षात्कार म॑ हुनी कहलकै कि हम्में अपनऽ फिजियोलॉजी के साथ काफी भाग्यशाली छियै लेकिन हमरा पृथ्वी केरऽ सर्वश्रेष्ठ यूनिट द्वारा भी प्रशिक्षित करलऽ गेलऽ छै । “त’ जखन अहाँ ओहि बात केँ सकारात्मक मानसिकता सँ जोड़ब त’ अहाँ किछुओ क’ सकैत छी।” पुरजा केरऽ जन्म २५ जुलाई १९८३ क॑ म्यागदी जिला केरऽ दाना गाँव म॑ भेलऽ छेलै, आरू पललऽ-बढ़लऽ बहुत हद तक चितवन म॑ भेलऽ छेलै । सैन्य सेवा केरऽ लंबा इतिहास वाला परिवार स॑ ऐलऽ छेलै : हुनकऽ पिता आरू तीन बड़ऽ भाई सब नेपाल केरऽ गोर्खा रेजिमेंट म॑ सेवा दै छेलै । पुर्जा स्वयं ओहि मार्ग पर चलल, छह साल ब्रिटिश गोर्खा के रूप मे सेवा देलक आ तखन ओ पहिल नेपाली बनल जे रॉयल नेवी के अभिजात इकाई ब्रिटिश स्पेशल बोट सर्विस मे स्वीकार केलक । ओ अपन पोथी मे लिखने छथि जे गोरखा बनब हमर एकमात्र सपना छल। “ई त’ एकमात्र काज छल जे हम कर’ चाहैत छलहुँ।” लगभग 16 साल केरऽ सैन्य कैरियर के दौरान, बाद म॑ एसबीएस केरऽ पहाड़ी इकाई के भीतर चरम ठंडा मौसम के युद्ध के विषय-वस्तु विशेषज्ञ बनलै । सैन्य सेवा आरू पर्वतारोहण केरऽ उपलब्धि लेली हुनका २०१८ म॑ ऑर्डर आफ द ब्रिटिश एम्पायर (एमबीई) केरऽ सदस्य नियुक्त करलऽ गेलऽ छेलै । ३० अक्टूबर २०१९ के भोर मे काठमांडू के त्रिभुवन अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय विमानस्थल हुनकर प्रतीक्षा मे पत्रकार सब स खचाखच भरल छल । पुरजा फूलक माला तर दबल आगमन हॉलसँ एतेक भारी निकलल जे मुश्किलसँ गरदनि हिला सकैत छल । ओहि अभियान के वित्तपोषण के लेल पुरजा स्पेशल बोट सर्विस सं इस्तीफा द देलखिन्ह, अपन सैन्य पेंशन छोड़ि देलखिन्ह आओर यूके मे अपन घर बेचि देलखिन्ह. ओहि समय ओ पत्रकार सब सं बातचीत मे कहलनि जे, हम यूनाइटेड किंगडम मे अपन नौकरी छोड़ि देलहुं, हम अपन पेंशन छोड़ि देलहुं आ एहि उच्च ऊँचाई, तेज गति क खोज लेल अपन घर बेचि देलहुं। “ककरो विश्वास नहि छल जे ई काज भ’ सकैत अछि, जखन हम प्रोजेक्ट पॉसिबल शुरू केने रही तखन सब हमरा पर हँसि रहल छल।” पुरजा कोनो पारंपरिक मार्ग स पर्वतारोहण मे नहि आयल छल । हुनकऽ पर्वतारोहण कैरियर केरऽ शुरुआत २०१२ म॑ एवरेस्ट बेस कैंप केरऽ ट्रेक स॑ शुरू होय छै, जेकरऽ योजना मूल रूप स॑ एगो साधारण पैदल यात्रा के रूप म॑ करलऽ गेलऽ छेलै, जेकरा हुनी शिखर धक्का म॑ विस्तारित करलकै, जेकरा बाद म॑ हुनी कहलकै कि ई अनुभव न॑ हुनकऽ पहाड़ऽ के महत्वाकांक्षा क॑ प्रज्वलित करी देलकै । आगू ओ ओहि बात केँ संकुचित केलनि जे आम तौर पर पर्वतारोही केँ साल वा दशक महीना मे लागि जाइत छैक । नेटफ्लिक्स केरऽ डॉक्यूमेंट्री “१४ पीक्स: नथिंग इज इम्पॉसिबल” म॑ वृत्तांत करलऽ गेलऽ हुनकऽ २०१९ केरऽ रिकॉर्ड तोड़ अभियान न॑ हुनका नेपाल, पाकिस्तान आरू तिब्बत भर म॑ ले गेलै, जेकरऽ समापन २९ अक्टूबर २०१९ क॑ शिशापांगमा के साथ करलऽ गेलै ।हुनकरऽ टीम म॑ मिंगमा डेविड शेर्पा, गेसमन तामांग, गल्जेन शेर्पा, लकपा डेंडी शेर्पा आरू हलुंग डोर्ची शेर्पा शामिल छेलै ।

फोटो : निर्मल पुरजा के फेसबुक से सौजन्य

पुरजा के लेल रिकॉर्ड कहियो खाली गति के नै छल। 23 अप्रैल, 2019 क॑ अन्नपूर्णा स॑ उतरतें हुअ॑ पुरजा न॑ अपनऽ खुद के अभियान क॑ बाधित करी क॑ मलेशियाई पर्वतारोही चिन वूई किन क॑ बचाबै म॑ मदद करलकै, जे लगभग 40 घंटा स॑ बिना खाना, पानी या पूरक ऑक्सीजन के फंसलऽ छेलै । पुरजा हुनका नीचा उतारलक, हालांकि बाद मे चिन के सिंगापुर निकालला के बाद हुनकर चोट सं मौत भ गेल. हफ्ता-हफ्ता बाद कंचेनजुंगा के आरोहण के दौरान पुरजा फेर दोसर के मदद के लेल अपन शिखर धक्का छोड़ि देलखिन्ह. ओ स्मरण करैत कहला जे 8450 मीटर पर हमरा सब कए अपन ऑक्सीजन देबय पड़ल आ तीनटा आओर पर्वतारोही कए बचाबय लागल। “ओ आत्महत्याक प्रयास छल आ संभवतः सबसँ कठिन क्षण।” अभियान म॑ हुनकऽ अंतिम बाधा मौसम या ऊंचाई स॑ नै बल्कि राजनीति स॑ छेलै : चढ़ै लेली खाली शिशापांगमा ही बची गेलऽ छेलै, चीनी अधिकारियऽ न॑ बार-बार हुनकऽ चढ़ाई के परमिट म॑ देरी करलकै, जेकरा आखिरकार १५ अक्टूबर क॑ बीजिंग के साथ कूटनीतिक हस्तक्षेप के बाद १५ अक्टूबर क॑ देलऽ गेलै । एकरऽ बाद पुरजा न॑ कहलकै कि उच्च ऊंचाई प॑ लोगऽ क॑ बचाबै स॑ ल॑ क॑ रस्सी ठीक करै तक, ऑक्सीजन के आपूर्ति स॑ ल॑ क॑ रूट खोलै आरू रात भर बिना सुतलऽ जाय तक, हम्मं॑ कई तरह के काम करी रहलऽ छेलियै आरू अपनऽ सीमा के परीक्षण करी रहलऽ छेलियै । “मुदा हम सभ डिलीवरी क’ देलियैक।” पुरजा न॑ ई करतब क॑ “अत्यंत, भयानक रूप स॑ अच्छा” कहलकै, रास्ता म॑ असफलता के बावजूद, जेकरा म॑ ल्होत्से प॑ चढ़ै के दौरान ओकरऽ ऑक्सीजन के आपूर्ति चोरी होय गेलऽ भी शामिल छेलै । वापसी के बाद काठमांडू में पत्रकार सब स बात करैत पुरजा कहलनि जे हुनका उम्मीद अछि जे हुनकर रिकॉर्ड अगिला पीढ़ी के नेपाली पर्वतारोही के ई देखाओत जे “संकल्प के संग सब किछु संभव अछि।” ऐसनऽ करतें हुअ॑ हुनी दक्षिण कोरियाई पर्वतारोही किम चांग-हो केरऽ पिछला सात साल, दस महीना आरू छह दिन के रिकॉर्ड क॑ तोड़ी देलकै आरू पोलिश पर्वतारोही केरऽ दिग्गज जेर्जी कुकुचका प॑ ग्रहण लगाय देलकै, जे लगभग आठ साल बाद १९८७ म॑ सब १४ आठ-हजार पूरा करै वाला पहलऽ व्यक्ति बनलऽ छेलै । पुरजा केरऽ अपनऽ रिकॉर्ड अल्पकालिक साबित होलै : २७ जुलाई २०२३ क॑ नार्वे केरऽ पर्वतारोही क्रिस्टीन हरिला आरू हुनकऽ नेपाली पर्वतारोही साथी टेंजेन (लामा) शेर्पा न॑ महज ९२ दिन म॑ सब १४ चोटी पूरा करी लेलकै । हुनकऽ २०१९ केरऽ कार्यक्रम अविश्वसनीय के सीमा म॑ पहुँची गेलऽ छेलै । ओ अन्नपूर्णा आ धौलागिरी चढ़ि कञ्चनजुंगा चलि गेलाह, फेर एवरेस्टक शिखर पर पहुँचलाह, तुरंत सटल ल्होत्से धरि पार केलनि, मकालू बेस कैंप पर उड़ि गेलाह आ मकालू पर चढ़ि गेलाह — ई सब 48 घंटाक भीतर. एकरऽ बाद हुनकऽ अभियान पाकिस्तान के माध्यम स॑ जारी रहलै, जहां हुनी नांगा परबत, गशरब्रम प्रथम, गशरब्रम द्वितीय, ब्रॉड पीक आरू के२ चढ़ी क॑ नेपाल वापस आबी क॑ मनसलू, चो ओयू आरू अंततः शिशापांगमा क॑ समाप्त करलकै । ओही अभियान के दौरान पुरजा एकटा फोटो खिंचौलनि जे दशक के परिभाषित पर्वतारोहण छवि में सं एक बनत : एवरेस्ट के शिखर के पास पर्वतारोही के एकटा लंबा कतार, जेकरा व्यापक रूप सं “ट्रैफिक जाम” कहल गेल छल, जे दुनिया भर में पहिल पन्ना पर चलैत छल, जाहि में द काठमांडू पोस्ट सेहो शामिल छल, आ नेपाल सरकार के चढ़ाई के नियम के कड़ा करय में मदद केलक. बाद म॑ हुनी मिंगमा डेविड शेर्पा के साथ एलिट एक्सपेड के सह-स्थापना करलकै आरू जनवरी २०२१ म॑ मिंगमा ग्यालजे शेर्पा के साथ-साथ १० सदस्यीय अखिल नेपाली टीम के हिस्सा छेलै, जेकरा न॑ के२ केरऽ पहिलऽ शीतकालीन आरोहण हासिल करलकै — हिमालयी पर्वतारोहण केरऽ आखिरी बिना दावा करलऽ गेलऽ मील के पत्थरऽ म॑ स॑ एक, जेकरा म॑ हुनी द पोस्ट क॑ बतैलकै कि ई चोटी १४ म॑ स॑ एकमात्र छेलै सच्चाई सॅं ओकरा डरा देलकैक। हुनकऽ ई यात्रा २०२१ म॑ नेपाल स॑ आगू के वैश्विक दर्शक वर्ग तलक पहुँचलै, जब॑ डॉक्यूमेंट्री “१४ पीक्स: नथिंग इज इम्पॉसिबल” न॑ १९१ देशऽ के दर्शकऽ क॑ नेपाल केरऽ पर्वतारोही समुदाय स॑ परिचित कराय क॑ पुरजा क॑ लगभग रातों-रात दुनिया केरऽ सबसें पहचानऽ वाला पर्वतारोही म॑ स॑ एक बनैलकै । पुरजा न॑ २०२० म॑ एगो संस्मरण, “बियॉन्ड पॉसिबल” प्रकाशित करलकै, जेकरा म॑ १६ साल के सैन्य कैरियर स॑ ल॑ क॑ रिकॉर्ड बनाबै वाला पर्वतारोही तक के रास्ता full_article:
KATHMANDU, AUGUST 1

Renowned Nepali-born British mountaineer Nirmal "Nimsdai" Purja has been confirmed dead after an avalanche claimed the lives of several climbers on Pakistan's Broad Peak, his company, Elite Exped, announced on Saturday.

Purja, 43, was leading a 10-member international expedition when the avalanche struck the 8,047-metre peak on Thursday, July 30, sweeping climbers down the mountain's west-facing gully.

Elite Exped in the social media confirmed that the avalanche claimed the lives of Purja and his trusted climbing partners Pur Bahadur Gurung (Yukta) and Nima Sherpa. The company also said other members of the expedition had not survived, while Pakistani authorities were continuing recovery and identification efforts.

In its tribute, Elite Exped described Purja as one of mountaineering's greatest climbers whose courage, leadership and determination inspired millions worldwide. It said his legacy would live on through the lives he touched and the organisations he built, including Elite Exped and the Nimsdai Foundation.

The avalanche hit the team as climbers were ascending from Camp II to Camp III, severing contact with the entire expedition.

On Friday, rescuers recovered four bodies from the mountain, two of which were identified as Nepali climber Pur Bahadur Gurung "Yukta" and Omani climber Nadhira Al Harthy. At the time, Purja, Kili Pemba Sherpa, Nima Sherpa, Nawang Thindu Sherpa, Gyalu Sherpa, Pakistan's Sohail Sakhi, Mallory Geis of the United States and Wang Zhong of China remained missing. Subsequent recovery and identification efforts led Elite Exped to confirm the deaths of Purja and his Sherpa teammates Pur Bahadur Gurung and Nima Sherpa.

Search operations resumed on Saturday after being suspended for a day due to severe weather and heavy snowfall. The Gilgit-Baltistan Administration said improved conditions had allowed helicopter sorties and ground search missions to continue, with additional Sherpa rescue teams joining the operation.

A three-member rescue team led by Nepal Mountaineering Association First Vice-President Mingma David Sherpa arrived in Pakistan to assist in the search, while a support team from the United Kingdom was expected to join shortly. The operation also involves Pakistan Army personnel, high-altitude rescue teams and veteran climbers. Ground teams led by renowned Nepali mountaineer Mingma Gyalje Sherpa (Mingma G) and Pakistani climber Sirbaz Khan have headed to locations identified through drone reconnaissance. According to Pakistani climber Naila Kiani, rescuers will first assess the avalanche zone to ensure it is safe from further slides before attempting any recovery.

The Government of Nepal, through its Embassy in Islamabad, has been coordinating closely with Pakistani authorities and the Alpine Club of Pakistan, while the Nepal Mountaineering Association and the Expedition Operators' Association Nepal have urged that every possible resource be mobilised for the mission.

The tragedy occurred just days after Purja summited Pakistan's Gasherbrum II on July 22, recording his 57th successful ascent of an 8,000-metre peak. The achievement had left him just one summit short of completing his ambitious Hat-Trick Project-climbing all 14 of the world's 8,000-metre peaks three times while also completing the Seven Summits three times.

नेपाल सरकार इस्लामाबाद स्थित अपन दूतावास के माध्यम स पाकिस्तानी अधिकारी आ पाकिस्तान के अल्पाइन क्लब के संग घनिष्ठ समन्वय करैत आबि रहल अछि, जखन कि नेपाल पर्वतारोहण संघ आ अभियान संचालक संघ नेपाल एहि मिशन के लेल हर संभव संसाधन जुटाबय के आग्रह केलक अछि।

पुरजा न॑ २२ जुलाई क॑ पाकिस्तान केरऽ गशरब्रम द्वितीय केरऽ शिखर प॑ पहुँचला के कुछ दिन बाद ही ई त्रासदी घटलै, जेकरा म॑ ८,००० मीटर के चोटी प॑ अपनऽ ५७वां सफल चढ़ाई दर्ज करलऽ गेलै । ई उपलब्धि स॑ हुनका अपनऽ महत्वाकांक्षी हैट्रिक प्रोजेक्ट पूरा करै म॑ महज एक शिखर के कमी छेलै-दुनिया केरऽ ८,००० मीटर केरऽ सब १४ चोटी प॑ तीन बार चढ़ै के साथ-साथ तीन बार सात शिखर सम्मेलन भी पूरा करै के मौका मिललऽ छेलै ।

The renowned Nepal-born British mountaineer Nirmal Purja is among those confirmed dead after his team were hit by an avalanche on Pakistan’s Broad Peak, according to the climber’s expedition company.

Purja was leading a 10-person expedition to summit Broad Peak, the world’s 12th tallest mountain located on the border with China, when the avalanche struck at midday on Thursday.

Elite Exped said in a statement on social media that the company “also received confirmation that other members of the expedition sadly did not survive”.

title: Koshi basin records fastest growth as Nepal’s glacial lakes expand - The Climate Watch
description: Koshi basin records fastest growth as Nepal’s glacial lakes expand  The Climate Watch
publisher.title: The Climate Watch
full_article:
The automated observatory could help authorities detect hazardous lake expansion earlier, supporting disaster risk reduction, hydropower planning and protection of downstream communities as Himalayan glaciers retreat.

Glacier-fed lakes across Nepal and its transboundary river basins increased in both number and size from 2017 to 2024, with the fastest expansion recorded in the Koshi basin, according to the first automated annual inventory of Himalayan glacial lakes developed by scientists.

Published in the peer-reviewed journal Earth System Science Data, the dataset is expected to improve the monitoring of potentially dangerous glacial lakes and strengthen early warning efforts against glacial lake outburst floods or GLOFs, one of the fastest-growing climate-related hazards in the Himalayas.

Researchers from the University of Leeds, Kathmandu University, the Wadia Institute of Himalayan Geology and the Chinese Academy of Sciences developed the Glacial Lake Observatory, or GLO, which uses satellite imagery and artificial intelligence to automatically detect and monitor glacial lakes each year.

Previous inventories depended heavily on manual mapping and were generally updated only once every several years. The new system instead uses deep-learning algorithms trained on thousands of satellite images collected by the European Space Agency’s Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 missions.

The method allows researchers to track changes more frequently and consistently, including in remote mountain regions where cloud cover often restricts optical observations.

“Fully automated and systematic monitoring of lake area changes has been lacking,” the researchers wrote, adding that continuous observation is essential for detecting unusually rapid lake expansion, estimating water storage and understanding glacier-lake interactions under a warming climate.

The study identified 4,150 unique glacial lakes using Sentinel-2 imagery and 2,967 lakes through Sentinel-1 radar observations across Nepal and neighbouring catchments in India and China.

Researchers mapped more than 22,000 individual lake outlines using Sentinel-2 imagery and more than 18,000 outlines from Sentinel-1 data collected between 2017 and 2024.

The combined dataset found that glacial lakes covered an average annual area of about 169 square kilometres. Both the number of lakes and their total area increased during the eight-year study period.

The Koshi River basin accounted for most of the expansion and contains about 61 percent of all mapped glacial lakes. Nine of the 10 fastest-expanding lakes identified by the study are within the basin, highlighting its growing vulnerability.

Researchers found that the expansion was concentrated mainly in high-elevation, glacier-fed lakes receiving meltwater directly from retreating glaciers.

The findings come as scientists warn that glaciers across the Hindu Kush Himalaya are melting at unprecedented rates, with regional temperatures rising much faster than the global average.

The paper said High Mountain Asia, often known as the “Third Pole” because it contains the world’s largest concentration of ice outside the Arctic and Antarctic, is warming at about twice the global average.

As glaciers lose mass, meltwater collects behind unstable moraine dams, forming and enlarging glacial lakes. Although the lakes temporarily store freshwater, they can fail catastrophically when triggered by avalanches, landslides or collapsing ice, releasing millions of cubic metres of water downstream within hours.

Glacial lake outburst floods have repeatedly damaged settlements, hydropower plants, roads and bridges in Nepal and neighbouring Himalayan countries.

The researchers warned that continued glacier retreat could increase both the number and size of hazardous lakes unless they are systematically monitored.

The research team developed the observatory by training a deep-learning model known as DeepLabV3 on manually mapped glacial lakes before applying it to satellite imagery covering the 2017-2024 period.

The system analyses radar and optical satellite images separately before combining the results.

Sentinel-1 radar imagery makes monitoring possible under cloudy conditions, while Sentinel-2’s higher-resolution optical imagery detects smaller lakes more accurately.

Validation showed that the automated mapping performed strongly, with F1 scores ranging from 0.80 to 0.92. Sentinel-2 consistently detected small lakes more effectively than radar imagery.

Researchers said using the two satellite systems together helped overcome one of the main obstacles to monitoring the Himalayas: persistent cloud cover during the monsoon.

The newly published dataset is openly available and will underpin a continuously updated Glacial Lake Observatory portal that is under development.

Scientists expect the database to support disaster risk reduction, glacier research, climate studies, hydropower planning and water resource management.

Because the process is fully automated, future updates can be produced regularly without requiring large teams to manually map thousands of lake boundaries.

“This provides the foundation for systematic glacial lake monitoring that does not require manual intervention,” the authors said.

Nepal has experienced several destructive glacial lake outburst floods in recent decades, while earlier studies have already identified dozens of potentially dangerous glacial lakes.

Scientists said continuous monitoring has become increasingly important for protecting downstream communities and critical infrastructure as climate change accelerates glacier retreat across the Himalayas.

The new observatory could also help authorities detect unusual lake expansion earlier, allowing more timely field investigations and risk assessments before catastrophic failures occur.

Researchers said the annual dataset marked only the first phase of the Glacial Lake Observatory. Future releases are expected to continue tracking changes in Himalayan glacial lakes as climate warming reshapes one of the world’s most sensitive mountain environments.

साथी द्वारा समीक्षित जर्नल अर्थ सिस्टम साइंस डाटा म॑ प्रकाशित ई डाटासेट स॑ संभावित खतरनाक हिमनदी झीलऽ के निगरानी म॑ सुधार आरू हिमालय म॑ सबसें तेजी स॑ बढ़तऽ जलवायु संबंधी खतरा म॑ स॑ एक हिमनदी झीलऽ के विस्फोट बाढ़ या जीएलओएफ के खिलाफ शुरुआती चेतावनी के प्रयास क॑ मजबूत करै के उम्मीद छै ।

लीड्स विश्वविद्यालय, काठमांडू विश्वविद्यालय, वाडिया इंस्टीट्यूट आफ हिमालयन जियोलॉजी आरू चीनी विज्ञान अकादमी के शोधकर्ता न॑ ग्लेशियल लेक ऑब्जर्वेटरी यानी जीएलओ के विकास करलकै, जेकरा म॑ उपग्रह केरऽ इमेजरी आरू आर्टिफिशियल इंटेलिजेंस के इस्तेमाल करी क॑ हर साल हिमनदी झीलऽ के स्वचालित रूप स॑ पता लगाय क॑ ओकरऽ निगरानी करलऽ जाय छै ।

पिछला इन्वेंट्री मैनुअल मैपिंग पर बहुत निर्भर छल आ आम तौर पर हर कई साल मे एक बेर मात्र अपडेट कैल जाइत छल । ई नया सिस्टम म॑ एकरऽ बदला म॑ यूरोपीय अंतरिक्ष एजेंसी केरऽ सेंटिनल-१ आरू सेंटिनल-२ मिशन द्वारा एकत्रित हजारों उपग्रह छवि प॑ प्रशिक्षित डीप-लर्निंग एल्गोरिदम के इस्तेमाल करलऽ गेलऽ छै ।

ई विधि शोधकर्ता सिनी क॑ परिवर्तन क॑ अधिक बार आरू लगातार ट्रैक करै के अनुमति दै छै, जेकरा म॑ दूरस्थ पहाड़ी क्षेत्र भी शामिल छै, जहां बादलऽ के आवरण अक्सर ऑप्टिकल अवलोकन क॑ सीमित करी दै छै ।

शोधकर्ता न॑ लिखलकै कि झील क्षेत्र म॑ बदलाव केरऽ पूर्ण रूप स॑ स्वचालित आरू व्यवस्थित निगरानी के कमी रहलऽ छै आरू कहलकै कि झील केरऽ असामान्य रूप स॑ तेजी स॑ विस्तार के पता लगाबै, पानी के भंडारण के अनुमान लगाबै आरू गरम होय रहलऽ जलवायु के तहत ग्लेशियर-झील के अंतःक्रिया क॑ समझै लेली लगातार अवलोकन जरूरी छै ।

अध्ययन म॑ सेंटिनल-२ इमेजरी के उपयोग करी क॑ ४,१५० अद्वितीय हिमनदी झील आरू सेंटिनल-१ रडार अवलोकन के माध्यम स॑ पूरा नेपाल आरू भारत आरू चीन केरऽ पड़ोसी जलग्रहण क्षेत्रऽ म॑ २,९६७ झील के पहचान करलऽ गेलऽ छै ।

शोधकर्ता न॑ सेंटिनल-२ इमेजरी आरू २०१७ आरू २०२४ के बीच एकत्रित सेंटिनल-१ केरऽ आंकड़ऽ स॑ १८,००० स॑ भी अधिक रूपरेखा के उपयोग करी क॑ २२,००० स॑ भी अधिक व्यक्तिगत झील के रूपरेखा के नक्शा बनैलकै ।

संयुक्त डाटासेट म॑ पता चललै कि हिमनदी झीलऽ के औसत वार्षिक क्षेत्रफल लगभग १६९ वर्ग किलोमीटर छै । आठ सालक अध्ययन अवधि मे झील क संख्या आ ओकर कुल क्षेत्रफल दुनू मे वृद्धि भेल ।

कोशी नदी बेसिन केरऽ अधिकांश विस्तार छेलै आरू एकरा म॑ लगभग ६१ प्रतिशत सब नक्शाबद्ध हिमनदी झील छै । अध्ययन द्वारा चिन्हित 10 सबसें तेजी स॑ विस्तारित झीलऽ म॑ स॑ नौ बेसिन के भीतर छै, जे एकरऽ बढ़तऽ कमजोरी प॑ प्रकाश डालै छै ।

शोधकर्ता सब के कहना छै कि ई विस्तार मुख्य रूप स॑ उच्च ऊंचाई वाला, ग्लेशियर स॑ भरलऽ झीलऽ म॑ केंद्रित छेलै जेकरा म॑ सीधा पीछे हटै वाला ग्लेशियरऽ स॑ पिघललऽ पानी मिलै छै ।

ई निष्कर्ष ऐन्हऽ समय म॑ सामने ऐलऽ छै जब॑ वैज्ञानिकऽ न॑ चेतावनी देल॑ छै कि पूरा हिन्दू कुश हिमालय केरऽ ग्लेशियर अभूतपूर्व दर स॑ पिघली रहलऽ छै, जेकरा म॑ क्षेत्रीय तापमान वैश्विक औसत स॑ बहुत तेजी स॑ बढ़ी रहलऽ छै ।

अखबार न॑ कहलकै कि हाई माउंटेन एशिया, जेकरा अक्सर “थर्ड पोल” के नाम स॑ जानलऽ जाय छै, कैन्हेंकि ओकरा म॑ आर्कटिक आरू अंटार्कटिक के बाहर दुनिया केरऽ सबस॑ बड़ऽ बर्फ के सांद्रता छै, वैश्विक औसत स॑ लगभग दू गुना तापमान प॑ गरम होय रहलऽ छै ।

जेना-जेना ग्लेशियर केरऽ द्रव्यमान कम होय जाय छै, अस्थिर मोरेन बांधऽ के पीछू पिघललऽ पानी जमा होय जाय छै, जेकरा स॑ हिमनदी झील बनी जाय छै आरू बढ़ी जाय छै । हालांकि ई झीलऽ म॑ अस्थायी तौर प॑ मीठा पानी के भंडारण होय छै, लेकिन हिमस्खलन, भूस्खलन या गिरै वाला बर्फ स॑ शुरू होय प॑ ई विनाशकारी रूप स॑ विफल होय सकै छै, जेकरा स॑ घंटऽ के भीतर लाखों घन मीटर पानी नीचें छोड़ी दै छै ।

हिमनदी झील फटला स बाढ़ि नेपाल आ पड़ोसी हिमालयी देश मे बेर-बेर बस्ती, जलविद्युत संयंत्र, सड़क आ पुल कए नुकसान पहुंचेलक अछि।

शोधकर्ता न॑ चेतावनी देलकै कि ग्लेशियर केरऽ पीछे हटला स॑ खतरनाक झीलऽ के संख्या आरू आकार दूनू बढ़ी सकै छै जब॑ तलक कि ओकरा प॑ व्यवस्थित नजर नै आबै ।

शोध टीम न॑ ई वेधशाला क॑ २०१७-२०२४ केरऽ अवधि क॑ कवर करै वाला उपग्रह इमेजरी प॑ लागू करै स॑ पहल॑ मैन्युअल रूप स॑ मैप करलऽ गेलऽ हिमनदी झीलऽ प॑ डीप-लर्निंग मॉडल क॑ प्रशिक्षित करी क॑ विकसित करलकै जेकरा क॑ डीपलैबवी३ के नाम स॑ जानलऽ जाय छै ।

ई सिस्टम परिणाम क॑ मिलाबै स॑ पहल॑ रडार आरू ऑप्टिकल उपग्रह केरऽ छवि के अलग-अलग विश्लेषण करै छै ।

सेंटिनल-1 रडार इमेजरी बादल वाला परिस्थिति म॑ निगरानी संभव बनाबै छै, जबकि सेंटिनल-2 केरऽ उच्च रिजोल्यूशन वाला ऑप्टिकल इमेजरी छोटऽ झीलऽ के अधिक सटीक रूप स॑ पता लगाबै छै ।

सत्यापन स॑ पता चललै कि स्वचालित मानचित्रण न॑ मजबूत प्रदर्शन करलकै, जेकरा म॑ एफ 1 स्कोर 0.80 स॑ 0.92 तलक रहलै । सेंटिनल-2 लगातार रडार इमेजरी स॑ भी अधिक प्रभावी ढंग स॑ छोटऽ झीलऽ के पता लगाबै छेलै ।

शोधकर्ता न॑ कहलकै कि ई दूनू उपग्रह प्रणाली के एक साथ इस्तेमाल करी क॑ हिमालय प॑ नजर रखै के एगो मुख्य बाधा क॑ दूर करै म॑ मदद मिललै: मानसून के दौरान लगातार बादलऽ के आवरण ।

नव प्रकाशित डाटासेट खुल क॑ उपलब्ध छै आरू ई लगातार अपडेट करलऽ जाय रहलऽ ग्लेशियल लेक वेधशाला पोर्टल के आधार बनतै जे विकास के दौर म॑ छै ।

वैज्ञानिक सब के उम्मीद छै कि ई डाटाबेस आपदा के जोखिम कम करै, ग्लेशियर रिसर्च, जलवायु अध्ययन, जलविद्युत योजना आरू जल संसाधन प्रबंधन के समर्थन करतै ।

चूँकि ई प्रक्रिया पूर्ण रूप स॑ स्वचालित छै, ई लेली भविष्य म॑ अपडेट नियमित रूप स॑ तैयार करलऽ जाब॑ सकै छै, जेकरा म॑ बड़ऽ टीम क॑ हजारों झील केरऽ सीमा के मैन्युअल रूप स॑ नक्शा बनाबै के जरूरत नै पड़ै छै ।

लेखकऽ न॑ कहलकै कि ई स॑ व्यवस्थित हिमनदी झीलऽ के निगरानी के आधार मिलै छै जेकरा म॑ मैनुअल हस्तक्षेप के जरूरत नै छै ।

नेपाल म॑ हाल के दशकऽ म॑ कईएक विनाशकारी हिमनदी झीलऽ के विस्फोट के बाढ़ के अनुभव होय चुकलऽ छै, जबकि एकरा स॑ पहल॑ के अध्ययनऽ म॑ दर्जनों संभावित खतरनाक हिमनदी झील के पहचान होय ​​चुकलऽ छै ।

वैज्ञानिक नँ कहलकै कि जलवायु परिवर्तन के कारण हिमालय भर मँ ग्लेशियर के पीछे हटै मँ तेजी आबै के कारण नीचे के समुदाय आरू महत्वपूर्ण बुनियादी ढाँचा के सुरक्षा लेली लगातार निगरानी के महत्व बढ़ी गेलौ छै ।

ई नया वेधशाला अधिकारियऽ क॑ असामान्य झील केरऽ विस्तार के पता लगाबै म॑ भी मदद करी सकै छै, जेकरा स॑ आपदाजनक विफलता स॑ पहल॑ अधिक समय पर क्षेत्रीय जांच आरू जोखिम के आकलन के अनुमति मिल॑ सकै छै ।

शोधकर्ता सब के कहनाय छनि जे वार्षिक डाटासेट ग्लेशियल लेक वेधशाला के पहिल चरण मात्र अछि. भविष्य म॑ रिलीज होय वाला हिमालयी हिमनदी झीलऽ म॑ बदलाव के ट्रैकिंग जारी रखै के उम्मीद छै, कैन्हेंकि जलवायु गर्मी स॑ दुनिया केरऽ सबसें संवेदनशील पहाड़ी वातावरण म॑ स॑ एक क॑ नया रूप देलऽ गेलऽ छै ।

title: Body of Nepali citizen who died in Kuwait attack being brought home - The Rising Nepal
description: Body of Nepali citizen who died in Kuwait attack being brought home  The Rising Nepal

full_article:
Kathmandu, Aug 1: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs has stated that the mortal remains of the Nepali citizen who died in the attack in Kuwait is being brought home.

The mortal remains of Nepali citizen, Som Kumar Tamang, a resident of Terhathum, who died in the attack in northern Kuwait on Thursday, is being brought to Nepal today via Kuwait Airways.

The ministry has expressed grief over this tragic incident and extended condolences to the bereaved family. The Nepali Embassy in Kuwait has stated that the process of sending the body home has been completed in coordination with the local authorities and the concerned recruitment companies. (RSS)

title: Security tightened along Bihar-Nepal border as unrest in Nepal amid fears of spill over - National Herald
description: Security tightened along Bihar-Nepal border as unrest in Nepal amid fears of spill over  National Herald
publisher.title: National Herald
full_article:
Security has been stepped up along the India-Nepal border in Bihar's Madhubani district following communal unrest in neighbouring Nepal, where violence has claimed at least three lives and prompted authorities to impose curfews in border districts.

Police said surveillance has been intensified across the international border as a precautionary measure to maintain peace and prevent any spillover of tension into Indian territory.

Communal clashes erupted in Sunsari district of Nepal's Koshi province last Sunday following a dispute over the use of loudspeakers during celebrations by two religious communities. The violence and subsequent police firing left at least three people dead and dozens injured.

The unrest has since spread to parts of Nepal, prompting authorities to impose curfews, prohibitory orders and deploy additional security personnel in several districts.

On Friday, Nepalese authorities imposed an indefinite curfew in parts of Saptari district in Madhesh province, which borders India.

नेपालके कोशी प्रदेशके सुनसरी जिल्लामे पछिला रविदिन दुटा धार्मिक समुदायके उत्सवके क्रममे लाउडस्पीकरके प्रयोगके विवादके बाद साम्प्रदायिक झड़प भेल अछि । हिंसा आ ओकर बाद पुलिसक गोलीबारी मे कम स कम तीन लोकक मौत आ दर्जनों लोक घायल भ गेल।

एकर बाद नेपालक किछु भाग मे अशांति पसरल अछि, जाहि सँ अधिकारि लोकनि कतेको जिला मे कर्फ्यू, निषेधात्मक आदेश आ अतिरिक्त सुरक्षाकर्मी तैनात केने छथि ।

शुक्रदिन भारतक सीमामे सटल मधेश प्रदेशक सप्तरी जिल्लाके किछु भागमे नेपाली अधिकारी अनिश्चितकालीन निषेधाज्ञा लगा देलक अछि ।

full_article:
Renowned mountaineer Nirmal Purja has been confirmed dead after an avalanche struck his expedition on Broad Peak in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK), his climbing company Elite Expeditions announced on Saturday.

“It is with profound sadness and immense heartbreak that we confirm that Nirmal Purja tragically lost his life following the avalanche on Broad Peak. We have also received confirmation that other members of the expedition sadly did not survive,” Elite Expeditions said in a statement on social media.

STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD

The avalanche hit on Thursday while the 10-member international team was attempting to summit Broad Peak, one of the world’s highest and most technically challenging mountains.

Contact with the climbers was lost shortly after the avalanche struck, triggering a large-scale rescue operation.

Nepal PM pays tribute

Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah expressed grief over Purja’s death, calling the tragedy deeply shocking.

“The tragic death of six Nepalese and four other foreign climbers, including world record holder Nirmal Purja, in the Karakoram mountain range… has shocked us,” Shah said in a statement on social media.

He added that although the climbers’ physical journey had ended, “the history of their courage, dedication, and contributions will always remain inspiring.”

Rescue efforts involving the Pakistani military, local high-altitude climbers and rescue teams have been hampered by severe weather and difficult terrain. Search operations resumed on Saturday after being temporarily suspended due to poor weather conditions.

The remains recovered so far have been flown by helicopter to a hospital for formal identification. Authorities said those recovered include an American woman, an Omani woman and a Nepali man.

A mountaineering legend

Purja, 43, was widely regarded as one of the world’s greatest high-altitude climbers. Before becoming a professional mountaineer, he served with Britain’s Brigade of Gurkhas and later joined the Royal Marines’ Special Boat Squadron.

He gained international recognition in 2019 after climbing all 14 mountains above 8,000 metres—known as the “eight-thousanders”—in just six months and six days, setting a world record at the time.

Earlier this week, Purja wrote on X that he was close to becoming the first climber to summit all 14 of the world’s “super peaks” twice without using supplemental oxygen.

“Broad Peak, I ask for nothing but safe passage up and back down,” he wrote.

Nepal-born British climber Nirmal Purja dies in avalanche on Pakistan’s Broad Peakx

Nepal-born British climber Nirmal “Nimsdai” Purja, famed for scaling all 14 of the world’s 8,000‑metre peaks in record time, was killed in an avalanche on Pakistan’s Broad Peak, along with other Nepali climbers, during an expedition on July 30.

Kathmandu: It was not originally part of famous climber Nirmal Purja’s plan to climb Pakistan’s Broad Peak, the 8,051-metre mountain in the Karakoram range. But the opportunity to make history prompted the Nepal-born British citizen to attempt one of the world’s highest peaks — a decision that ended in tragedy when he was killed in an avalanche that struck Broad Peak on Thursday, the company he founded confirmed on Saturday.

“Today, it is with profound sadness and immense heartbreak that we confirm that Nirmal ‘Nimsdai’ Purja tragically lost his life following the avalanche on Broad Peak,” Elite Exped, the company founded by Purja, wrote on its Facebook page.

“We have also received confirmation that other members of the expedition sadly did not survive.”

The company said other members of the expedition, including Pur Bahadur Gurung (Yukta) and Nima Sherpa, also lost their lives.

“Our deepest thoughts, prayers and heartfelt condolences are with their families, friends and loved ones,” it said.

Nepal’s Prime Minister Balendra Shah also expressed deep condolences, confirming that all Nepali climbers attempting Broad Peak — Pur Bahadur Gurung (“Yukta”), Kili Pemba Sherpa (“Kilu”), Nima Sherpa, Nawang Thindu Sherpa and Gyalu Sherpa besides Nirmal Purja (“Nims Dai”) — had lost their lives.

“The tragic deaths of six Nepali climbers, including world record-holding mountaineer Nirmal Purja (Nims Dai), along with four foreign climbers on the 8,051-metre Broad Peak — the world’s 12th-highest mountain, located in Pakistan’s Karakoram Range — have left us deeply shocked and saddened,” Shah wrote on his Facebook page.

“Although the physical journey of Nirmal Purja and all the departed climbers has come to an end, their courage, dedication and contributions will continue to inspire generations and remain forever alive in history,” he added.

Shah said that while the mountains reward many with the glory of reaching their summits, they sometimes embrace climbers in their bosom forever.

“Yet, mountaineers remain immortal in history through their courage and dedication,” he wrote.

Purja was part of an expedition on Broad Peak when an avalanche struck the team on July 30.

Mingma Gyabu Sherpa, a member of Nepal’s House of Representatives and Purja’s business partner, had earlier said tracking data showed Purja’s position had shifted after the avalanche — first appearing to have been swept downhill before moving again to the point where the signal eventually stopped.

In 2019, Purja stunned the mountaineering world by climbing all 14 of the world’s 8,000-metre peaks in just over six months under his ‘Project Possible’, shattering the previous record of nearly eight years.

By summiting Broad Peak, he hoped to become the first person in history to climb all 14 eight-thousanders twice, a goal that motivated him to attempt the mountain.

Before the tragedy, Purja revealed in a Facebook post on July 27 that Broad Peak had not been part of his original plan, as he had intended to climb only Gasherbrum II (G2). However, an opportunity to summit Broad Peak arose, and he did not want to miss the chance to make history.

“This was never the plan. Initially, the plan was to climb just G2. But just before setting off for Pakistan, I ran the numbers on my 8,000m summits. That’s when it hit me: if I tick off Broad Peak whilst I’m here, only one remains — Cho Oyu. Then I become the FIRST person in history to climb all 14 eight-thousanders twice. Without oxygen,” he wrote.

But his dream of making history ended in tragedy.

Born in Nepal’s Dhaulagiri region and raised in Chitwan, Purja served for 16 years in the military, including six years with the British Gurkhas and a decade with the United Kingdom’s elite Special Boat Service (SBS), becoming the first Gurkha to join the special forces unit.

Purja took up mountaineering only in 2012 after trekking to Everest Base Camp while on military leave. In 2018, he set a world record by climbing Mount Everest, Lhotse and Makalu in just five days. The following year, he completed all 14 of the world’s 8,000-metre peaks in just over six months.

Known for his exceptional ability to acclimatise rapidly at extreme altitude, Purja also led numerous high-altitude rescue missions, earning global recognition not only for his climbing achievements but also for saving lives in the Himalayas.

Elite Exped said the world had lost one of mountaineering’s greatest climbers — a leader who inspired millions through his courage, humility and unwavering belief that human potential is far greater than people often imagine.

“More than his extraordinary achievements, he wanted to show the world what was possible when you dared to dream bigger, believed in yourself and refused to accept limitations. Through his actions, he inspired millions of people to believe that they, too, could achieve more than they ever thought possible,” the company said.

काठमांडू : ई मूल रूप स॑ प्रसिद्ध पर्वतारोही निर्मल पुरजा केरऽ काराकोरम श्रृंखला केरऽ ८,०५१ मीटर केरऽ पहाड़ पाकिस्तान केरऽ ब्रॉड पीक प॑ चढ़ै के योजना के हिस्सा नै छेलै । लेकिन इतिहास रचय के मौका न॑ नेपाल म॑ जन्मलऽ ब्रिटिश नागरिक क॑ दुनिया केरऽ एगो उच्चतम चोटी के कोशिश करै लेली प्रेरित करलकै — ई फैसला के अंत त्रासदी म॑ होय गेलै जब॑ गुरुवार क॑ ब्रॉड पीक प॑ आईल हिमस्खलन म॑ ओकरऽ मौत होय गेलै, ई बात के पुष्टि हुनकऽ स्थापना करलऽ कंपनी न॑ शनिदिन करलकै ।

पुर्जा द्वारा स्थापित कंपनी एलिट एक्सपेड अपन फेसबुक पेज पर लिखलक अछि जे, आइ गहींर उदासी आ अपार दिल टूटला स हम सब एहि बात क पुष्टि करैत छी जे ब्रॉड पीक पर हिमस्खलन क बाद निर्मल ‘निम्सदाई’ पुरजा क दुखद रूप स जान गंवा देलथि।

“हमरा सब क॑ ई बात के पुष्टि भी मिललऽ छै कि ई अभियान केरऽ अन्य सदस्य दुखद रूप स॑ नै बचलै ।”

कंपनी के कहनाय अछि जे एहि अभियान के दोसर सदस्य, जाहि मे पुर बहादुर गुरुंग (युक्त) आओर निमा शेर्पा सेहो शामिल अछि, हुनकर जान सेहो चलि गेल छल.

ओहि मे कहल गेल अछि जे, हमर सबहक गहींर विचार, प्रार्थना आ हार्दिक संवेदना हुनकर परिवार, मित्र आ प्रियजन क संग अछि।

नेपाल केरऽ प्रधानमंत्री बलेन्द्र शाह न॑ भी गहरी शोक व्यक्त करी क॑ ई बात के पुष्टि करलकै कि ब्रॉड पीक केरऽ प्रयास करै वाला सब नेपाली पर्वतारोही — पुर बहादुर गुरुंग (“युक्ता”), किली पेम्बा शेर्पा (“किलू”), निमा शेर्पा, नवांग थिंदू शेर्पा आरू ग्यालु शेर्पा के अलावा निर्मल पुरजा (“निम्स दाई”) — के जान गेलऽ छै ।

शाह न॑ अपनऽ फेसबुक प॑ लिखलकै कि ८,०५१ मीटर केरऽ ब्रॉड पीक — पाकिस्तान केरऽ काराकोरम रेंज म॑ स्थित दुनिया केरऽ १२वां सबसें ऊंचऽ पहाड़ — प॑ विश्व रिकॉर्ड बनै वाला पर्वतारोही निर्मल पुरजा (निम्स दाई) सहित छह नेपाली पर्वतारोही के दुखद मौत न॑ हमरा सब क॑ गहराई स॑ चौंका आरू दुखी करी देल॑ छै पृष्ठ।

हुनी आरू कहलकै, “हालांकि निर्मल पुर्जा आरू सब दिवंगत पर्वतारोही के भौतिक यात्रा के समापन होय ​​गेलौ छै, लेकिन हुनकौ साहस, समर्पण आरू योगदान पीढ़ी-दर-पीढ़ी प्रेरित करतै आरू इतिहास मँ हमेशा लेली जिंदा रहतै ।

शाह कहलनि जे, पहाड़ जतय बहुतो के अपन शिखर तक पहुंचय के गौरव के पुरस्कृत करैत अछि, ओतहि ओ कखनो काल पर्वतारोही के हमेशा के लेल अपन कोरा में गले लगा लैत छथि।

ओ लिखलनि जे, तइयो पर्वतारोही अपन साहस आ समर्पणक माध्यमे इतिहास मे अमर रहैत छथि।

पुरजा ब्रॉड पीक पर एकटा अभियान के हिस्सा छल जखन 30 जुलाई के टीम पर हिमस्खलन भेल छल.

नेपाल केरऽ प्रतिनिधि सभा के सदस्य आरू पुर्जा केरऽ व्यापारिक भागीदार मिंगमा ग्याबू शेर्पा न॑ पहल॑ भी कहल॑ छेलै कि ट्रैकिंग डाटा स॑ पता चलै छै कि हिमस्खलन के बाद पुरजा केरऽ स्थिति बदली गेलऽ छै — पहल॑ ही ऐन्हऽ लगै छेलै कि ओकरा नीचें बहाय देलऽ गेलऽ छेलै आरू ओकरा बाद फेरू स॑ ऐसनऽ बिंदु प॑ पहुँची गेलै जहाँ अंततः सिग्नल बंद होय गेलै ।

2019 म॑ पुरजा न॑ अपनऽ ‘प्रोजेक्ट पॉसिबल’ के तहत दुनिया केरऽ 8,000 मीटर केरऽ सब 14 चोटी प॑ छह महीना स॑ कुछ अधिक समय म॑ चढ़ी क॑ पर्वतारोहण दुनिया क॑ स्तब्ध करी देलकै, जेकरा स॑ लगभग आठ साल केरऽ पिछला रिकॉर्ड क॑ तोड़ी देलकै ।

ब्रॉड पीक केरऽ शिखर प॑ पहुँची क॑ हुनका आशा छेलै कि हुनी इतिहास केरऽ पहलऽ व्यक्ति बन॑ सक॑ जे दू बार सब १४ आठ-हजार चढ़ी गेलऽ छेलै, जेकरा स॑ हुनका पहाड़ केरऽ प्रयास करै लेली प्रेरित करलऽ गेलै ।

त्रासदी स॑ पहल॑ पुरजा न॑ २७ जुलाई क॑ फेसबुक पोस्ट म॑ खुलासा करलकै कि ब्रॉड पीक हुनकऽ मूल योजना के हिस्सा नै छेलै, कैन्हेंकि हुनकऽ इरादा छेलै कि हुनी खाली गशरब्रम द्वितीय (जी२) प॑ चढ़ै । मुदा, ब्रॉड पीक पर चढ़बाक अवसर भेटल, आ ओ इतिहास रचबाक मौका नहिं छोड़य चाहैत छलाह.

ओ कहला जे इ कहियो योजना नहि छल। शुरू मे योजना छल जे सिर्फ जी2 पर चढ़ब। मुदा पाकिस्तान जेबा स ठीक पहिने हम अपन 8000 मीटर शिखर पर नंबर दौड़लहुं। तखने हमरा पर लागल: जँ हम एत’ रहैत ब्रॉड पीक पर टिक लगाबी त’ मात्र एकटा बचल अछि — चो ओयू. तखन हम इतिहास मे पहिल व्यक्ति बनैत छी जे दू बेर सब 14 आठ-हजार पर चढ़ल छी। बिना ऑक्सीजन के।'' ओ लिखलनि।

मुदा इतिहास रचबाक हुनकर सपना त्रासदी मे समाप्त भ गेलनि।

नेपाल केरऽ धौलागिरी क्षेत्र म॑ जन्मलऽ आरू चितवन म॑ पललऽ-बढ़लऽ पुरजा न॑ १६ साल तलक सेना म॑ काम करलकै, जेकरा म॑ छह साल ब्रिटिश गोर्खा सिनी के साथ आरू एक दशक यूनाइटेड किंगडम केरऽ कुलीन विशेष नाव सेवा (एसबीएस) के साथ छेलै, जेकरा स॑ विशेष बल इकाई म॑ शामिल होय वाला पहिलऽ गोर्खा बनलै ।

पुरजा न॑ सैन्य छुट्टी प॑ एवरेस्ट बेस कैंप म॑ ट्रेकिंग के बाद ही २०१२ म॑ ही पर्वतारोहण के काम शुरू करलकै । 2018 म॑ माउंट एवरेस्ट, ल्होत्से आरू मकालू प॑ चढ़ी क॑ महज पांच दिन म॑ विश्व रिकॉर्ड बनैलकै । अगिला साल ओ दुनिया के 8000 मीटर के सभ 14 चोटी के छह महीना सं किछ बेसि समय मे पूरा क लेलखिन्ह.

चरम ऊंचाई पर तेजी स॑ अभ्यस्त होय के असाधारण क्षमता लेली जानलऽ जाय वाला पुरजा न॑ उच्च ऊंचाई प॑ अनेक बचाव मिशन के नेतृत्व भी करलकै, जेकरा स॑ न सिर्फ अपनऽ चढ़ाई के उपलब्धि लेली बल्कि हिमालय म॑ जान बचाबै लेली भी वैश्विक पहचान मिललै ।

एलिट एक्सपेड न॑ कहलकै कि दुनिया न॑ पर्वतारोहण केरऽ एगो महान पर्वतारोही क॑ खो देल॑ छै — एगो ऐसनऽ नेता जे अपनऽ साहस, विनम्रता आरू अटूट विश्वास के माध्यम स॑ लाखों लोगऽ क॑ प्रेरित करलकै कि मानवीय क्षमता लोगऽ के कल्पना स॑ कहीं अधिक छै ।

“अपनऽ असाधारण उपलब्धि स॑ भी जादा वू दुनिया क॑ ई देखाबै ल॑ चाहै छेलै कि जब॑ आपने बड़ऽ सपना देखै के हिम्मत करबै, खुद प॑ विश्वास करै छियै आरू सीमा क॑ स्वीकार करै स॑ मना करी दै छियै त॑ की संभव छै । अपनऽ हरकत के माध्यम स॑ हुनी लाखों लोगऽ क॑ ई मानै लेली प्रेरित करलकै कि वू भी, जेतना कुछ संभव नै सोचलऽ छेलै, ओकरा स॑ भी अधिक हासिल करी सकै छै ।'
